![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14058907/assets/f7bacafcbe893c0d21ea45a916190a49aa3a3532834cff4704f707c100bf8e6a.png)

Which of the following is equivalent to the integral ${\int }_{C}F(r)\cdot \text{d}r,$ where $F(x,y)=3y\,i+2x\,j$ and $C$ is the the arc of the ellipse centered at the origin with horizontal and vertical semiaxes $1$ and $3$ respectively, traversed anticlockwise from $A(0,3)$ to $B(-1,0)?$

*Hint: Use the parametrization $r(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j.$*
worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

First, we need to find the parametrization of an ellipse centered at the origin with horizontal and vertical semiaxes $1$ and $3$ respectively. It can be parametrized as 

$$
r(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j,\,\frac{\pi }{2}\le t\le \pi .
$$

So, along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,y=3\operatorname{sin}⁡t.
$$

As a result,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =3y\,i+2x\,j \\  & =9\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{sin}⁡t)j \\  & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+3\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(9\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j)\cdot (-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+3\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j) \\  & =-9{sin}^{2}⁡t+6{cos}^{2}⁡t \\  & =6{cos}^{2}⁡t-9{sin}^{2}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can write the integral as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F(r)\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }(6{cos}^{2}⁡t-9{sin}^{2}⁡t)\,dt.\end{aligned}
$$
